scope: Matching original DLL/PDB static evidence, unmodified original Lua source, and separate portable Mac scheduler observations. No original game execution, Android device or emulator work.

observed_source_contract.ownership: Main.lua owns Lua coroutines, timer/event queues, tag cancellation and deferred presentation. Native reconstruction invokes its real functions.
observed_source_contract.initial_resume: dispatch and thread create a Lua coroutine and immediately call original resume. The callback runs until completion, error or first positive/event wait.
observed_source_contract.timed_waits: wait(nil), wait(0), wait(negative) return immediately. Positive wait yields a table and queues an absolute world-clock deadline; waitScreenTime uses screen clock.
observed_source_contract.strict_deadline: Main.update resumes only when resumeTime < selected clock, not <=. A frame exactly equal to deadline does not resume the coroutine.
observed_source_contract.event_waits: waitUntil consumes a retained event once or yields into the event listener table. notify resumes current listeners synchronously; if none, it retains an event for a future wait. notifyExistingWaiters never retains a missing event. Listeners resumed by notify append later waits to _workingThreads.
observed_source_contract.tagged_cancellation: killTaggedThreads queues tags; update excludes due threads marked for killing and removes matching remaining waits after queue rotation. killWaitUntilThreads deletes one event listener list. killAllWaitingThreads resets timed/working/event queues.
observed_source_contract.frame: update(time,screenTime) first computes world elapsed and replaces the source globals, calls optional UpdateTimers(elapsed), traverses timed waits, rotates _workingThreads, applies cancellation, then calls draw(time,screenTime). draw calls deferred combat, UI and audio functions.
observed_source_contract.ordering_caution: The original Lua code uses pairs and can start other threads during a resume. The bridge leaves those exact source operations unchanged rather than imposing a replacement scheduling order.
observed_source_contract.fault: Original resume checks coroutine.resume status, logs DebugMessage and asserts failure. A native protected update failure sets ScriptManager::HAS_CRASHED; portable frame bridge latches its failure and refuses silent retries of partially mutated state.

arguments.native_type: float, PDB type0x40, converted to Lua number

native_frame_contract.cached_function: ScriptManager::LUA_UPDATE retains the original Lua function; replacing a global later does not replace the bridge cached function.
native_frame_contract.world_clock: World::Update multiplies supplied float frame delta by world time scale then accumulates float mElapsedTime at0x180315074/07a and increments mFrame. Clock generation, scale easing and pause/step ownership remain parent engine integration work.
native_frame_contract.screen_clock: ScreenManager::Update accumulates float frame delta converted to double into s_ElapsedTime at0x1801a7aef..af7. Focus/update early-out paths still apply; it is not an unconditional wall clock.
native_frame_contract.pause: World non-running or paused without mStepFrame returns before ScriptManager::Update. Distinct screen-clock deadlines do not by themselves establish Lua resumes while native world updates are suppressed.
native_frame_contract.native_delayed_actions: Before invoking Lua update, native ScriptManager processes separate FireData/ScriptAction records (0xa0-byte records, deadline+0x98) and executes only when worldTime > deadline. The new portable Lua bridge does not implement this distinct engine-action queue.
native_frame_contract.gc_and_thread_guard: Native also performs Cleanup, Lua GC step and one-thread access guards; these are not claimed as reconstructed by the new scheduling bridge.

properties: VM-owned registry table caches original Lua function values; no original Lua mutation.
Finite caller-supplied clocks, stack preservation, queue diagnostics and explicit retained faults.
Parent controls world activation, frame/pause clocks, native delayed-action execution, actor components and engine notifications.
limits: Does not create actors, execute native delayed actions, update camera/physics, play audio or provide save persistence.
Public notify helper accepts named string events as an integration seam; it does not reproduce every native condition/check action producing events.

checks: world-clock held while screen-clock supplied advances
synchronous event resume and working-queue handoff
cached update retained after global replacement
nonfinite clock rejected without corrupting state
expected coroutine error preserved and further frame attempts blocked
portable_validation.limits: Synthetic callback bodies and instrumented deferred hooks establish scheduling semantics only, not complete room/gameplay integration.

session_lifecycle.reason: Reused exact matching retained REA evidence and supplemented it with bounded original DLL disassembly and matching PDB declarations; no new native session required.

unknowns: Full native delayed engine-action queue scheduling/reentrancy integration.
Complete host clock, pause, focus and step behavior around every screen mode.
Actual RoomOpening scheduling requires real actors, remaining engine interfaces, source data state and proper ordered callback dispatch.
